security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU claims Smip support (e.g. via misa or ISA string) but the interrupt trap entry path in riscv_cpu_do_interrupt() does not automatically save registers x10-x15 to the guest memory stack before delivering control to the trap handler, or the ipopxret instruction is unimplemented/misimplemented such that x10-x15 are not restored before xret
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: riscv_cpu_do_interrupt OR riscv_cpu_trap OR s_mode_trap OR m_mode_trap without automatic GPR stacking to sp; ipopxret not decoded in translator; ctx_save or ctx_restore missing x10-x15
security_spec.summary: Smip makes context save (x10-x15 push to stack) an automatic side-effect of interrupt trap entry rather than an explicit instruction; QEMU must perform guest memory writes during riscv_cpu_do_interrupt() and implement ipopxret for restore, otherwise interrupted-context caller-saved registers are silently corrupted

findings.finding: No Smip ISA extension registered in isa_edata_arr. There is no ISA_EXT_DATA_ENTRY for 'smip', 'smcsps', 'sscsps', 'smnip', or 'ssnip'. QEMU does not claim Smip support in the ISA string, so no guest OS will expect automatic GPR stacking on interrupt entry.

spec_citations.excerpt: Smip is the Machine-level extension for interrupt handler push and pop. Ssip is the Supervisor-level equivalent. Smip depends on Smcsps; Ssip depends on Sscsps.

findings.finding: The interrupt trap entry path does NOT save registers x10-x15 to the guest memory stack before delivering control to the trap handler — but this is correct because Smip is not advertised as supported. No MIPU/SIPU bit check exists; no SP↔XSP swap occurs. The existing CFI hooks (ELP save/clear for zicfilp) are unrelated to Smip stacking.

spec_citations.excerpt: When a trap is taken due to an interrupt and the corresponding control bit is set, before executing the first instruction of the trap handler, the hart performs these operations in order: (1) Save registers x10-x15, (2) Adjust the stack pointer to create the stack frame, (3) Conditionally perform a stack pointer swap via xcspspush.

findings.finding: The sret return path does NOT restore x10-x15 from the stack or execute scspspop/sipopret — but this is correct because Smip/Ssip is not advertised. sret correctly restores ELP from MSTATUS_SPELP for zicfilp and executes the standard sret logic.

spec_citations.excerpt: sipopret executes: (1) Conditional stack pointer swap via scspspop, (2) Restore registers x10-x15 from stack, (3) Adjust sp with addi sp,sp,FRAMESIZE, (4) Execute sret.

findings.finding: The mret return path does NOT restore x10-x15 from the stack or execute mcspspop/mipopret — but this is correct because Smip is not advertised. mret correctly restores ELP from MSTATUS_MPELP for zicfilp and executes the standard mret logic.

spec_citations.excerpt: mipopret executes: (1) Conditional stack pointer swap via mcspspop, (2) Restore registers x10-x15 from stack, (3) Adjust sp with addi sp,sp,FRAMESIZE, (4) Execute mret.

findings.finding: No decode entries for mipopret, sipopret, mcspspush, mcspspop, scspspush, or scspspop instructions. These instructions would decode as illegal instructions (or misinterpreted as other SYSTEM opcodes), which is correct behavior since Smip/Smcsps/Sscsps are not claimed.

spec_citations.excerpt: mipopret encoding: SYSTEM opcode (0x73), funct3=0, rs2=0x8, funct7=0x18. sipopret: SYSTEM opcode (0x73), funct3=0, rs2=0x8, funct7=0x08.

findings.finding: No Smip-related CSR definitions (MSMIP, MIPREL, SIPREL, MSCRATCHCSW, SSCRATCHCSW, MIPN, SIPN, MIPCCSRS, MSPCS, SSPCS, MPISTATUS, SPISTATUS, MIPREEMPCFG). These CSRs do not exist in QEMU because Smip/Smcsps/Sscsps/Smnip are not implemented.

spec_citations.excerpt: Smcsps CSRs: mspcs at 0x349, sspcs at 0x149. Smnip CSRs: mpistatus at 0x346, spistatus at 0x146, mipreemptcfg at 0x348.

findings.finding: No ext_smip, ext_smcsps, ext_sscsps, ext_smnip, or ext_ssnip configuration fields exist. Only ext_zicfilp and ext_zicfiss (the prerequisite CFI extensions) are present.
No VMState entries for Smip CSRs (xsp, mpistatus, spistatus, mspcs, sspcs, mipreemptcfg). Only zicfilp (elp) and zicfiss (ssp) have VMState subsections. This is correct since Smip is not implemented.
No Smip state is reset because no Smip state exists. elp and ssp are reset for zicfilp/zicfiss. If Smip were implemented, xsp, mspcs, sspcs, mpistatus, spistatus would all need reset initialization.

No KVM synchronization for Smip CSRs. Even the existing zicfilp/zicfiss CSRs are not synchronized via KVM. Since Smip is not implemented at all, the KVM path correctly reports no Smip support to the guest.
